_o: Rozsirujici slovnik k data/jazyky.json. Klic = PRESNY cesky text z appky, hodnota = preklad. Nacita se AZ po prepnuti jazyka (js/jazyky.js, loadExtra) a jen pro zvoleny jazyk, aby cestina nestahovala nic navic. Zaznam, ktery uz je v jadre (data/jazyky.json), se odsud NEPOUZIJE — jadro ma prednost.

t.Helmertova lokalizace není aktivní — nej: Helmert localisation is not active — switch it on in Tools first.
t.Dočasné zviditelnění bodu pro měření — v: Temporary way to make a point visible for measuring — a pole, a target, a reflective tag.
t.Přístroj na přesné měření vodorovných a: An instrument for precise measurement of horizontal and vertical angles (without a rangefinder).
t.• Android / Chrome: ikona zámku v adresn: • Android / Chrome: the lock icon in the address bar → Permissions → Camera.
t.Vybrané body nejsou v aktivním hledání v: The selected points are not visible in the active search — clear the search or select others.
t.Pomocný měřický bod pro připojení podrob: An auxiliary survey point used to connect a detailed survey. Shown in the app as a circular symbol.
t.Vybrané body už byly lokalizací srovnány: The selected points have already been aligned by localisation (each point is recalculated only once).
t.Stabilizace bodu ocelovým hřebem, typick: Stabilisation of a point with a steel nail, typically in a kerb, rock or paved surface.
t.Spojnice dvou bodů, od níž se ortogonáln: A line between two points from which detailed points are determined orthogonally (chainage + perpendicular offset).
t.Čáry mezi body v mapě a AR — nejsou to u: Lines between points on the map and in AR — they are not saved points. Deleting a link does not delete the points.
t.Zadej posun jako „ΔY ΔX\" nebo „ΔY ΔX ΔZ: Enter the shift as "ΔY ΔX" or "ΔY ΔX ΔZ" in metres, separated by a space — e.g. "0 0 -0.05".
t.Technický podklad a dokumentace měření p: Technical basis and survey documentation for changes in the cadastre (the basis of a surveying plan).
t.Úhlová jednotka běžná v geodézii: pravý: An angular unit common in surveying: a right angle = 100 gon, a full circle = 400 gon. 1 gon = 0.9°.
t.Kód se propíše do CSV/TXT/DXF exportu (v: The code is written into the CSV/TXT/DXF export (in DXF as a drawing layer). A dash "-" removes the code.
t.Souhrnné označení globálních družicových: A collective term for global navigation satellite systems: GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou.
t.Právo k cizí nemovitosti zapsané v KN (n: A right to someone else's property recorded in the cadastre (e.g. a utility line, right of way, servitude).
t.Závazný výškový systém ČR; nadmořské výš: The binding height system of Czechia; elevations referenced to the Baltic Sea level (1957 adjustment).
t.Dvojité kuželové konformní zobrazení v o: A double conical conformal projection in an oblique position, the basis of S-JTSK. Designed by Josef Křovák (1922).
t.Souhrn geodetických bodů na území státu:: The set of geodetic control points of the country: horizontal (TB, ZhB, PBPP), vertical (levelling) and gravimetric.
t.Bod doplňující (zhušťující) síť trigonom: A point supplementing (densifying) the network of trigonometric points. Shown in the app as a blue square.
t.Posun v metrech S-JTSK: „ΔY ΔX\" nebo „Δ: A shift in metres of S-JTSK: "ΔY ΔX" or "ΔY ΔX ΔZ" (space separated). E.g. to lower the height by 5 cm: "0 0 -0.05".
t.Přenesení polohy bodů (např. hranice poz: Transferring the position of points (e.g. a plot or building boundary) from the documentation into the field — the opposite of surveying.
t.Síť permanentních GNSS stanic spravovaná: A network of permanent GNSS stations run by the national survey office; it provides corrections for RTK measurement in Czechia.
t.Silné světlo — zapnul jsem venkovní reži: Strong light — I switched on outdoor mode (higher contrast). To turn it off: Settings → Display and legibility.
t.Pozemek, který je geometricky a polohově: A parcel of land that is geometrically and positionally determined, shown in the cadastral map and marked with a parcel number.
t.Veřejný seznam obsahující soupis, popis: A public register containing the list, description and geometric and positional determination of real estate, including the rights to it.
t.Základní báze geografických dat ČR — dig: The fundamental geographic database of Czechia — a digital topographic model of the country run by the national survey office.
t.Technická jednotka, kterou tvoří místopi: A technical unit formed by a topographically closed set of properties recorded together in the cadastre.
t.Řada navazujících bodů, mezi nimiž se mě: A series of connected points between which distances and angles are measured; used to determine the coordinates of new points.
t.Evropský terestrický referenční systém —: The European Terrestrial Reference System — the realisation of a coordinate system for precise GNSS measurement in Europe.
t.Výpis z katastru prokazující vlastnictví: An extract from the cadastre proving ownership; it lists owners, properties, restrictions and notes in the given cadastral district.
t.Bonitovaná půdně ekologická jednotka — p: A soil-ecological rating unit — a five-digit code expressing the quality of agricultural land (it affects the price).
t.Metoda GNSS měření s korekcemi v reálném: A GNSS measurement method with real-time corrections (from a reference station or a network). Accuracy at the centimetre level.
t.Určení polohy bodu staničením (podél měř: Determining a point by chainage (along a survey line) and a perpendicular offset; historically common, still used in sketches.
t.Elektronický přístroj měřící vodorovné i: An electronic instrument measuring horizontal and vertical angles as well as distances (rangefinder); the basic tool of detailed survey.
t.Grafický doklad o vytyčení hranice pozem: A graphic record of a boundary stakeout; together with the report it is handed to the owners and documents the stakeout.
t.Určení polohy bodu měřením směru (úhlu): Determining a point by measuring a direction (angle) and a distance from a station. Today the most common method of detailed survey.
t.Zařízení neposkytuje absolutní azimut –: The device does not provide an absolute azimuth – north may be inaccurate. Fine-tune it in the compass settings under "North alignment".
t.Výškový rozdíl mezi dvěma body. V aplika: The height difference between two points. In the app it is computed by the Distance measurement tool (from GPS heights — indicative only).
t.Kameru právě drží jiná aplikace nebo ji: The camera is being held by another app, or the system could not start it. Close other apps using the camera and try again.
t.Úředně oprávněný zeměměřický inženýr — o: An officially authorised surveying engineer — a person entitled to certify the results of surveying activities (surveying plans, stakeouts…).
t.Kámen nebo plastový znak trvale stabiliz: A stone or plastic marker permanently stabilising a boundary corner of a plot. The head is usually marked with a cross or a dimple.
t.Registr územní identifikace, adres a nem: The register of territorial identification, addresses and real estate — one of the country's basic registers (addresses, streets, parcels, buildings).
t.Český úřad zeměměřický a katastrální — s: The Czech Office for Surveying, Mapping and Cadastre — the administrator of the cadastre, control networks, orthophoto and other data the app uses.
t.Úhel mezi magnetickým a zeměpisným sever: The angle between magnetic and true north. In Czechia currently roughly +5° to +6° east and growing; the app corrects for it automatically.
t.Rozdíl mezi elipsoidickou výškou (GPS) a: The difference between the ellipsoidal height (GPS) and the elevation above sea level (Bpv). In Czechia roughly 44–47 m; the app subtracts it when computing heights.
t.Zadej PRVNÍ název série (musí končit čís: Enter the FIRST name of the series (it must end with a number). The selected points get consecutive numbers in the order of the list; numbers already taken are skipped.
t.Trvalé osazení bodu v terénu: kámen (mez: Permanent marking of a point in the field: a stone, nail, pipe, bolt, chiselled cross. The "stabilisation" attribute of a point tells you what to look for in the field.
t.Měření převýšení mezi body pomocí nivela: Measuring the height difference between points with a level and staffs. Geometric levelling from the middle is the most accurate common method of height determination.
t.Vodorovný úhel měřený od severu po směru: A horizontal angle measured from north clockwise: 0–360° or 0–400 gon. The app shows it in the HUD (tap to switch units).
t.Světový geodetický systém používaný GPS: The world geodetic system used by GPS — latitude and longitude on an ellipsoid. The phone's GPS returns the position in it; the app converts it to S-JTSK.
t.Technický podklad pro zápis změny do kat: The technical basis for recording a change in the cadastre (dividing a plot, recording a building, an easement…). Certified by an authorised surveyor and confirmed by the cadastral office.
t.Bod výškového bodového pole se známou na: A point of the vertical control network with a known elevation (Bpv). Marked with a bolt or nail plate, e.g. on buildings and bridges. Shown in the app as a red ring.
t.Bod základního polohového bodového pole: A point of the fundamental horizontal control network with precisely determined coordinates. In the field usually a granite prism with a cross, often protected by a concrete ring. Shown in the app as a purple triangle.
t.Systém Jednotné trigonometrické sítě kat: The system of the Unified Trigonometric Cadastral Network — the binding coordinate system of Czechia (Křovák projection). Coordinates Y and X in metres; mathematically negative, in practice written as positive (Y ~ 430–905 km, X ~ 935–1230 km).

t.Sourozenci z jedné rodiny (ICON-D2, ICON: Siblings from one family (ICON-D2, ICON-EU and their ensembles are still one DWD model) are first averaged among themselves and only then enter the whole with one vote — otherwise one institute would have several times the weight and "Source agreement" would report false certainty.
t.U zdrojů se „ensemble\" počítá průměr ze: For the sources marked "ensemble" the average of all the runs of that model is computed (ECMWF 51, ICON-D2 20 …) — it tends to be more accurate than a single run. For PRECIPITATION the median is taken instead of the mean, so that a sharp shower does not get smeared into drizzle, and the ensembles moreover give an honest probability of rain (in what percentage of the runs it rains). The weights are computed separately for a range up to 6 hours and separately beyond it — ICON-D2 is the best for the short range, ECMWF for a longer one. The ensembles are downloaded at most once an hour so as not to burn mobile data.

t.Slovní stav nahoře vychází z tohohle pro: The verbal state at the top comes from this percentage of sky cover (weighted mean of all models): up to 12 % clear, up to 50 % mostly clear, up to 88 % partly cloudy, above that overcast. Earlier the models voted on the category and it was enough for a few to say "overcast" to override the majority — which is why "overcast" sometimes showed on a sunny day. When it is raining according to the radar or a ČHMÚ rain gauge, the observation takes precedence over everything.
t.Váhy se počítají jako 1/σ² ze změřené ch: Weights are computed as 1/σ² from the source's measured error, as in a survey adjustment: a source twice as accurate gets four times the weight, not a third more. While there are few evaluations, the weight stays near its a-priori value so a few random hits don't throw it off. Outlying sources are also EXCLUDED — via median and MAD (not mean and standard deviation, which an outlier distorts itself and hides in), threshold 3×MAD and never discarding the majority. For precipitation nothing is excluded: its distribution is skewed, so a heavy shower looks like an outlier even when true. "Source agreement" is computed BEFORE exclusion, otherwise it would report false certainty exactly where the weather is uncertain. Where a systematic error (bias) is known, it is SUBTRACTED — a model that is consistently a degree too warm here gets corrected, not just down-weighted. The bias is kept SEPARATELY FOR FOUR PARTS OF THE DAY (night, morning, day, evening): models tend to run warm at night and cold in the afternoon peak, and one number for the whole day would average the two errors to zero. While a part of the day has few measurements, the overall bias is blended in so the correction doesn't jump with noise. The daily maximum is corrected by the afternoon bias, the minimum by the night bias.

t.Jak ji najít: prodluž zadní stěnu Velkéh: How to find it: extend the back wall of the Big Dipper (from Merak through Dubhe) five times — the first brighter star is Polaris. Its height above the horizon = your latitude.

t.Hvězdy jsou nejstarší geodetická síť: az: The stars are the oldest geodetic network: azimuth from Polaris, latitude from its height above the horizon, longitude from the time a star crosses the meridian — that is how Laplace points and S-JTSK were oriented. Polaris is within 1° of the pole, the rest is computed from time; the magnetometer lies by degrees, Polaris does not. In the app: Compass → Check by Polaris.

t.AR umisťuje značky na obrazovku podle zo: AR places markers on screen according to the camera’s field of view. If it’s wrong, points in the centre of the image fit but drift apart towards the edges. The wizard measures it using azimuth — one distant landmark is enough.
t.<b>Než začneš:</b> běž ven, zkalibruj ko: Before you start: go outside, calibrate the compass (figure-eight with the phone) and pick a distant isolated object — a mast, chimney, house corner. It must be farther than ~50 m, otherwise your own movement creeps into the measurement. Keep the phone in place and only rotate it.
t.Nejrychlejší cesta. Výrobce u fotoaparát: The fastest way. The manufacturer states the camera’s focal length as a 35 mm equivalent — e.g. “main 26 mm”. Enter it and the angle comes out by itself. No compass or landmark needed.
t.Když kompas zlobí: postav se kolmo k dlo: If the compass misbehaves: stand square to a long wall at a known distance D. Mark the spots on the wall that lie exactly at the left and right edges of the image and measure the width W between them. Then FOV = 2 · arctan(W / 2D). For example W = 4.00 m at D = 3.00 m gives 67.4°. Then enter the value with the slider in Settings → AR camera → Advanced.
t.Zorný úhel <b>{h}° × {v}°</b> je nastave: Field of view {h}° × {v}° is set from the {f} mm focal length. t.<b>Proč to jde.</b> Chyba GPS v telefonu: Why it works. A phone's GPS error is not random scatter around the right spot — at any given moment it is mainly one vector (say 2 m to the north-east) arising in the ionosphere, the troposphere and the satellite orbits. That vector changes slowly (over quarter-hours) and within a few hundred metres it is almost the same for every phone. Professional DGPS/RTK relies on exactly this: a reference station on a known point measures how far GPS is off and the rover subtracts it. Here the "reference station" is your walk along a known edge.
t.<b>Jak to appka počítá.</b> Každý fix GP: How the app computes it. It projects every GPS fix during the walk onto the nearest line segment and computes the cross-track offset (how far GPS puts you beside the line, minus your side offset). If 40 fixes are on average 2.3 m left of the edge, GPS is off by 2.3 m to the right — and that is subtracted from new points. Gross jumps (reflection off a building) are rejected (3× MAD); the scatter of the rest gives the correction error estimate. On a straight line only the component perpendicular to the line is visible — along it any point would fit equally well, so the along-track component stays zero. That is why for a road it is ideal to walk along the kerb: the cross component is the one that matters when laying out. On a bent line (curve, corner ≥ 30°) the full vector comes out.
t.<b>Na jakou přesnost se dá dostat.</b> C: What accuracy you can reach. Correction error ≈ fix scatter ÷ √(independent fixes) ⊕ accuracy of the line itself. In practice: 30–50 m of walking with ±3–5 m fixes gives the perpendicular component to ±0.3–0.5 m; with a good signal and 80 m of walking ±0.2 m. A line tapped from the map adds the basemap error (ČÚZK orthophoto ~0.2–0.5 m, street map even more) — an edge from DXF or from points you know has no such error. So from a bare phone (±3–5 m) you get to half a metre perpendicular to the edge — not RTK, but usually enough for laying out, checking an edge or finding a point. You see the error estimate with the result. Fixes are weighted by their accuracy (±3 m counts 16× more than ±12 m), gross jumps are rejected. Most accurate is to walk there and back: you don't hold the phone exactly above your track (in your right hand it is 0.2–0.4 m to the right) and walking back flips that error — so the app separates it from the real GPS error.
t.<b>Jak dlouho to platí.</b> Korekce má h: How long it is valid. The correction has a monitored validity of 20 min and 300 m from where you walked: once on, a pill at the top shows "GPS correction · X min left · Y m from the spot" (green = valid, orange = nearing the limit, red = beyond the limit) and the app warns you 5 min before expiry, at expiry, at 200 m and at 300 m. It does not switch the correction off by itself — if you know GPS is calm today you can keep measuring, the app just no longer vouches for it. To renew, simply walk the edge again (on the way back is fine).
t.<b>Uzavřený tvar místo přímky.</b> Na ro: A closed shape instead of a straight line. On a straight line only the perpendicular component comes out; when you walk around a corner, a square, a plus sign or a whole plot perimeter (tap "Close shape" or tap back on the first point), the segments point in different directions and you get the full vector. The app also compares the first and second half of the walk — how much the GPS error drifted during the walk (for a loop this equals the misclosure). Above 1 m it is a restless day: calibrate more often.
t.<b>Kalibrace před a po.</b> Chyba GPS me: Calibration before and after. The GPS error drifts between two walks (typically 0.5–1 m in 20 min). If you walk the edge before and after measuring (within 90 min and 500 m), the app offers to recompute by time the points saved in between: a point measured in the middle gets half the difference of the two vectors, a point right after the first walk almost nothing. The error doesn't drift linearly, so this cuts the drift roughly in half — but it is the cheapest improvement there is. Each point carries what it received, so the vector is replaced, not added (also for Precise GPS). Changes go to the journal.
The correction is only as accurate as the line's source. ČÚZK orthophoto ±0.2–0.5 m (a sharp edge on the ground: kerb, asphalt edge, foot of a wall — not a roof, which is shifted in the photo), cadastral boundary in DKM ±0.14–0.3 m (a fence often isn't on it), saved or imported points ±cm, street map ±1–5 m = unsuitable for calibration. The line accuracy is added to the error estimate and you see it with the result.
